summary: Sunday run based on the latest available arXiv daily listing, Friday 11 Sep 2026. The strongest selected theme is heavy-ion jet-medium response, with a fast wake prescription benchmarked against full hydrodynamics. Additional high-value items concern physics-guided Gaussian-process priors for nuclear inference, multiplicity-dependent non-flow in RHIC-energy pp, light-nucleus and hypernucleus production systematics, measurement combinations with constrained nuisance parameters, and transferable warnings about detector-defined ML labels.
strongest_paper: arXiv:2609.10679, Computationally Efficient Description of Medium Response to Jets in Heavy Ion Collisions
top_takeaway: A benchmarked, computationally cheap treatment of jet-induced QGP wakes could materially improve heavy-ion jet Monte Carlo phenomenology if it remains accurate in realistic backgrounds.

papers.title: Computationally Efficient Description of Medium Response to Jets in Heavy Ion Collisions
papers.authors: Jorge Casalderrey-Solana, Jose Guilherme Milhano, Daniel Pablos, Krishna Rajagopal, Xiaojun Yao
papers.abstract: Develops an Efficient Wake procedure for jet wakes in heavy-ion collisions using reusable linearized hydrodynamics templates, benchmarked against full 3+1D hydrodynamics with large speedups.

papers.title: Nuclear-physics-guided Gaussian Processes
papers.authors: Javier Rozalen Sarmiento, Hristijan Kochankovski, Arnau Rios, Angels Ramos
papers.abstract: Encodes nuclear-physics structures into Gaussian-process priors for phase shifts, mass excesses, and dense-matter EOS, reporting better interpolation, calibration, and extrapolation than agnostic baselines.

papers.title: Study of the multiplicity dependence of non-flow correlations in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=200 GeV using PYTHIA
papers.abstract: Uses PYTHIA to show RHIC-energy pp multiplicity selections bias jet-related non-flow correlations and challenge simple subtraction procedures.

papers.title: Production of Light Nuclei and Hypernuclei in Heavy-Ion Collisions
papers.abstract: Reviews STAR and ALICE results on light nuclei and hypernuclei, emphasizing coalescence, femtoscopy, flow, wave-function sensitivity, feed-down, and production chronology.

papers.title: Hunting the Unseen: Deep Learning Analysis for Semi-Visible Jet Tagging
papers.authors: Miguel A. Avendano-Bernal, Srinandan Dasmahapatra, Ahmed Hammad, Stefano Moretti, Mihoko Nojiri, Michael H. Seymour, Claire Shepherd-Themistocleous
papers.abstract: Benchmarks deep-learning representations for semi-visible jet tagging, finding global kinematics strong and multimodal combinations best overall.

papers.title: Combinations of measurements that are simultaneous fits of parameters of interest and systematic uncertainties using the BLUE method
papers.authors: Tomas Dado, Mark Owen, Michele Pinamonti
papers.abstract: Extends BLUE combinations to simultaneous estimates of parameters of interest and nuisance parameters, with pseudo-experiment validation and open-source implementation.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Drift Diagnosis for Laser-Plasma Accelerator Operations
papers.authors: Ou Labun, Calin Hojbota, Mara Klebonas, Mike Downer, Rafal Zgadzaj, Phil Franke, Lance Labun
papers.abstract: Uses an extended Kalman filter latent state-space model for drift diagnosis in laser-plasma accelerator operation, validated in synthetic sessions.

papers.title: Prevalence Determines Precision: Silent Contamination in Detector-Defined Datasets
papers.authors: Jia Huang, Yankai Wan, Yangjun Ou
papers.abstract: Shows detector-defined dataset precision is governed by pool-level true-positive prevalence, with large phantom-rate variation across candidate pools.

papers.title: Bayesian Superiority in On/Off analysis
papers.abstract: Compares Bayesian criteria with Li-Ma On/Off analysis under selected priors and simulated backgrounds, claiming lower error rates for Jeffreys prior.
